newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fazio, bankers see room for loan rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fazio, bankers see room for loan rate cuts.

text.p: Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio and major Italian bankers see room to reduce the range of bank lending rates which would bring down the average cost to clients of borrowing money.

This was the sentiment which emerged from a regular weekly meeting between the central bank and major credit institutions which focused on the need to review the current structure of bank loan and deposit rates, sources said.

"The bankers agreed with the governor that under current conditions the possibility existed for a narrowing of the broad range of loan rates banks offer which would permit a reduction in clients' average borrowing costs," the sources said.
Earlier on Thursday, Prime Minister Romano Prodi called on Italian banks to cut lending rates, saying low inflation was not enough to guarantee economic recovery.

The meeting of bankers expressed satisfaction over the confirmation today that November consumer price inflation fell to 2.6 percent year-on-year from 3.0 percent in October, the lowest rate since June 1969.
But there was some concern that the current economic situation remained weak due to falling investments and insufficient growth in demand, the sources said.

The extent of a European recovery was still uncertain and in any case had only a limited impact on Italian production activity. Italian industry still appeared to be competitive, however, given current exchange rates, according to Bank of Italy studies.

Economic prospects for 1997 were based on "moderately positive indications" for the international cycle and on an expected upturn in private investment in Italy as well as hopes that state initiatives would get underway, especially in the poor south of the country, if administrative obstacles could be overcome, the sources added.
